summary: Discussed how to extend web UI for the globally installed subagents and workflows Pi extensions. Settled on a rule that UI must never ship without its extension, leading to a 'sibling web bundle' design: each Pi extension in the agent dir can carry a sibling .web.js file discovered and served by Gizmo via extensions.web, keyed by the extension file's stem.
decisions: UI must never ship without its Pi extension — globally installed Pi extensions must be able to carry their own web UI alongside the .ts file in the agent directory, rather than living in a separate Gizmo package.

Pairing key for a Pi extension's web bundle is the extension file's stem (e.g., ask-user.ts ↔ ask-user.web.js), and Gizmo must discover sibling .web.js files alongside Pi extension paths (agent-dir + seeded) and serve them via extensions.web, deduped against Gizmo extensions and builtins.

ask_user's web UI moves out of the app's static builtins and becomes a seeded ask-user.web.js beside ask-user.ts, re-joining the pair per the rule; the chat question card itself remains a shell-generic bridge renderer.
Web bundles reuse the existing GizmoWebExtension contract (id, labels, resultFor, inspectorTabs, etc.), so subagents/workflows UI can be authored against the same shape without forking Gizmo.
